If an unused weak function was traced
column2: it's call to fentry will still

column1: exist
column2: which gets added into the __mcount_loc table. Ftrace will use

column1: kallsyms to retrieve the name for each location in __mcount_loc to display
it in the available_filter_functions and used to enable functions via the
name matching in set_ftrace_filter/notrace. Enabling these functions do
nothing but enable an unused call to ftrace_caller. If a traced weak
function is overridden
column2: the symbol of the function would be used for it

column1: which will either created duplicate names
column2: or if the previous function was

column1: not traced
column2: it would be incorrectly be listed in available_filter_functions

column1: as a function that can be traced.
This became an issue with BPF[1] as there are tooling that enables the
direct callers via ftrace but then checks to see if the functions were
actually enabled. The case of one function that was marked notrace
was followed by an unused weak function that was traced. The unused
function's call to fentry was added to the __mcount_loc section
kallsyms retrieved the untraced function's symbol as the weak function was
overridden. Since the untraced function would not get traced
check would detect this and fail.
The real fix would be to fix kallsyms to not show addresses of weak
functions as the function before it. But that would require adding code in
the build to add function size to kallsyms so that it can know when the
function ends instead of just using the start of the next known symbol.
In the mean time
column2: this is a work around. Add a FTRACE_MCOUNT_MAX_OFFSET

column1: macro that if defined
column2: ftrace will ignore any function that has its call

column1: to fentry/mcount that has an offset from the symbol that is greater than
FTRACE_MCOUNT_MAX_OFFSET.
If CONFIG_HAVE_FENTRY is defined for x86
to zero (unless IBT is enabled)
column2: which will have ftrace ignore all locations

column1: that are not at the start of the function (or one after the ENDBR
instruction).
A worker thread is added at boot up to scan all the ftrace record entries
and will mark any that fail the FTRACE_MCOUNT_MAX_OFFSET test as disabled.
They will still appear in the available_filter_functions file as:
__ftrace_invalid_address___<invalid-offset>
(showing the offset that caused it to be invalid).
This is required for tools that use libtracefs (like trace-cmd does) that
scan the available_filter_functions and enable set_ftrace_filter and
set_ftrace_notrace using indexes of the function listed in the file (this
is a speedup
column2: as enabling thousands of files via names is an O(n^2)

column1: operation and can take minutes to complete
than a second).
The invalid functions cannot be removed from available_filter_functions as
the names there correspond to the ftrace records in the array that manages
them (and the indexing depends on this).
